## H07 Ohm's law

Ohm's law describes the relationship among voltage, current, and resistance for a component or network under the stated operating conditions.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![Ohm's law triangle with voltage above current and resistance.](../schematics/Ohms_Law_Triangle.svg){width=48%}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![Ohm's law triangle with voltage above current and resistance.](../schematics/Ohms_Law_Triangle.pdf){width=48%}
:::

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|:--:|:--|:--|
| $V$ | potential difference | volt, $\mathrm{V}$ |
| $I$ | current | ampere, $\mathrm{A}$ |
| $R$ | resistance | ohm, $\Omega$ |

**Worked GUESS example**

| Step | Entry |
|:--:|:--|
| G | $V=12.0\ \mathrm{V}$ |
| G | $R=680\ \Omega$ |
| U | current, $I$, in amperes |
| E | $I=V/R$ |
| S | $I=12.0/680$ |
| S | $I=0.0176\ \mathrm{A}$ |
| S | $I=17.6\ \mathrm{mA}$ |

**Casio entry**

`12.0 ÷ 680 =`

**Common mistake:** Do not apply one component's voltage across a different component. Mark the two nodes that define each voltage.

**Application and links:** LED resistors, sensors, lamps, heaters, and conductors. [Ohm's law notes](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/02-basic-electronics/03-ohms-law.html).

```{=latex}
\newpage\markright{H08 Power and energy}
```

## H08 Power and energy

Power is the rate of energy transfer. A design must keep every component below its voltage, current, and power limits with an appropriate margin.

$$P=VI=I^2R=\frac{V^2}{R} \qquad E=Pt$$

**Worked GUESS example:** A $12.0\ \mathrm{V}$ lamp draws $0.50\ \mathrm{A}$. $P=(12.0)(0.50)=6.0\ \mathrm{W}$. In $2.0\ \mathrm{h}$ it uses $12\ \mathrm{Wh}$.

**Casio sequence**

`12.0 × 0.50 =`

`Ans × 2.0 =`

**Warning:** A component with the correct resistance can still overheat if its power rating is too low.

**Application and links:** Power supplies, battery runtime, wire heating, and resistor selection. [Power and energy notes](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/02-basic-electronics/04-power-energy.html).

```{=latex}
\newpage\markright{H09 Series circuits}
```

## H09 Series circuits

Series components form one current path. The same current passes through every series component, while the source voltage divides among them.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![Series circuit with one path and the same current through both resistors.](../schematics/Series_Rule_Reference.svg){width=68%}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![Series circuit with one path and the same current through both resistors.](../schematics/Series_Rule_Reference.pdf){width=68%}
:::

$$I_T=I_1=I_2 \qquad V_T=V_1+V_2 \qquad R_T=R_1+R_2$$

**Worked GUESS example:** $R_1=220\ \Omega$ and $R_2=330\ \Omega$ on $9.0\ \mathrm{V}$. $R_T=550\ \Omega$ and $I_T=9.0/550=16\ \mathrm{mA}$.

**Common mistake:** Components are not in series when another branch leaves their shared node.

**Application and links:** Strings of components, current sensing, and voltage division. Use the basic-circuit worksheet from the [electronics library](https://andrewandrade.ca/tech-edu-resources/tej3-4/electronics-library/).

```{=latex}
\newpage\markright{H10 Parallel circuits}
```

## H10 Parallel circuits

Parallel branches connect to the same two nodes, so every branch has the same voltage. Total current is the sum of branch currents.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![Parallel circuit with separate branches and the same voltage across both resistors.](../schematics/Parallel_Rule_Reference.svg){width=68%}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![Parallel circuit with separate branches and the same voltage across both resistors.](../schematics/Parallel_Rule_Reference.pdf){width=68%}
:::

$$V_T=V_1=V_2 \qquad I_T=I_1+I_2 \qquad \frac{1}{R_T}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}$$

**Worked GUESS example:** $R_1=1.0\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$ and $R_2=2.0\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$ on $10.0\ \mathrm{V}$. $I_1=10\ \mathrm{mA}$, $I_2=5.0\ \mathrm{mA}$, and $I_T=15\ \mathrm{mA}$.

**Common mistake:** The equivalent resistance must be smaller than the smallest branch resistance.

**Application and links:** Household branches, vehicle accessories, computer loads, and multiple indicators. Use the parallel-load activity in the basic-circuit worksheet.
